conclusions.causal_assessment: The retained evidence establishes variable elapsed measurements on the fixed workload. It does not identify the cause. Unchanged LLVM/driver binaries and unchanged normalized Rust logic rule out an observed source/LLVM artifact regression; Rust binary hashes differ and their old temporary artifacts are not available for text-section comparison. No causal claim of external load, frequency variation, scheduling contention, or missed background jobs is justified without historical telemetry.
conclusions.load_average_limit: Load averages are host aggregates with historical smoothing, not per-sample CPU-0 scheduling evidence. The earlier passing scalar run even records higher load averages than the failing scalar run, so increased host load is not established as an explanation.
conclusions.sampling_policy: No pooling, clipping, cross-run selection, or extra measurement was performed.
conclusions.scope_limit: No bug in metric recomputation or incorrect rejection was found. Failing the specified quality gate remains a real release-qualification blocker; earlier passes and favorable time ratios cannot replace these complete inconclusive attempts.
conclusions.second_owned: Real measurement-quality rejection: constructor_error/rust MAD 0.07851365132992036 and constructor_error/llvm MAD 0.06160656380472986 > 0.05; no speed-threshold violation.
conclusions.second_scalar: Real measurement-quality rejection: branch_accumulate/rust relative MAD 0.10323094311498651 > 0.05; no speed-threshold violation.
